budgets.reason: Prevent earlier lanes or projects from silently starving later members of an explicit authority set.

verification.selector: Exact cross-project permissions, isolation, ranking, budgets, timeout/cancellation, provenance, schema parity, and two-real-PV integration
Parallel, cross-lane, and cross-project query stack
Lane guidance, reader, lane contract, registry, and packaged-skill integration
Python lint, compile, schema parse, and whitespace validation
verification.result: Ruff, py_compile, json.tool, and git diff --check passed

negative_cases: A cross-project query cannot discover projects implicitly or weaken the default single-project route.
Every member requires a unique canonical project ID and exact accepted PV reference; candidate identities are rejected.
Missing, malformed, mismatched, or unsealed permission grants fail closed before project reads.
Lane timeouts cannot exceed the enclosing project timeout, and project timeout/cancellation remains explicit in the receipt.
Each project aggregate must cover all declared lane-query limits, and the overall aggregate must cover all declared project limits.
A result missing project, PV, lane, ref, path, locator, source hash, or chunk hash provenance fails closed.
Completion timing and raw retrieval scores cannot merge independent project rank domains.
No project SQLite, lane SQLite, PV package, Plan backlog, raw FTS corpus, or lineage database is placed in model context.
limitations: Row218 supplies the internal cross-project query primitive; SDK handler parity remains Row219.
Public skill and MCP routing remains Row221.
The separate historical TASK_CONTRACT_AMENDED projection regression remains outside Row218.
next_boundary: Close Row218 through its exact per-Delta checkpoint. Row219 EL-CODEX-T6-PARITY-022-SDK-HANDLER-PARITY owns effect-correct SDK handler registration, ABI narrowing, provider adapters, and production-construction tests.
